quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?
questions.explanation: Many types of drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on state highways unless otherwise posted?
questions.explanation: The default speed limit on state highways is 55 mph. Follow posted signs if a different speed limit is shown.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leaving plenty of space between you and other vehicles gives you enough time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When is it safe to use cruise control?

options.text: When driving in rural areas with light traffic
When driving in heavy rain and snow

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving in rural areas with light traffic
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic, near many exits and entrances, or on wet or slippery roads. This can distract you and increase crash risk. Do not use cruise control when towing heavy loads.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, signal first, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: When parallel parking, how close should your wheels be to the curb?
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels within 12 inches of the curb when parallel parking. Park only where traffic is clear and your vehicle is visible from all directions.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, where should you look?

options.text: The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an oncoming vehicle does not dim its high beams. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle approaching from the right
The vehicle approaching from the left
The vehicle whose driver honks first

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle approaching from the right
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, a driver must yield to any vehicle approaching from the right.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed
Prepare to stop because the light is about to turn red

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Look both ways before driving through the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on overcast days?

options.text: Do not turn on any lights

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles or within 500 feet of vehicles ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: The person is a police officer.

questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, what is the minimum distance you should stay behind another car?
questions.explanation: Keep three to four seconds between your car and the car ahead. This gives you time to react if something goes wrong. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Honk your horn to alert the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light marks a dangerous intersection. Treat it the same way you treat a stop sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
You must come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down at a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before any crosswalk.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give the pedestrian the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give the pedestrian the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right.

questions.question: What do orange signs tell you about?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about work zones. They are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols and tell you people are working on or near the road.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so you cannot see as well as during the day. Use your headlights from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.

questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road shows where the edge is. It marks the boundary between the travel lane and the shoulder. If the line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious motor vehicle crash?
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Check if anyone is hurt. Call 911 if someone is injured. You must report the crash to police if anyone is injured, if someone dies, or if there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What is the correct way to drive on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. Eating before drinking can slow alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: You are waiting at an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to ask drivers to let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before crossing. Another train may be approaching on a different track.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: When may you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with traffic.

questions.question: What traffic light comes after a steady yellow light?
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear soon.

questions.question: When you see another car with bright headlights coming toward you, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car is coming toward you with high beams on, look away from the bright lights and toward the right side of the road. Keep looking there until the car passes. This stops the bright lights from blinding you.

questions.question: What can affect how quickly you can stop your car?
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how fast you can stop. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or damaged so you can keep control. If you go too fast on slippery roads and need to stop, you could lose control.

questions.question: You can pass another car if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines divide traffic lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass another car if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show laws that drivers must always follow. When this sign is posted, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow. Orange diamond signs are used in work areas. These signs warn you about dangers ahead or areas where special rules apply.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the gas pedal, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic if your right wheels leave the road. Release the gas pedal and steer the car parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and turning gently into the right lane. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Circular traffic signs warn of railroad crossings. This sign tells you a railroad crossing is coming and you should look for trains.

questions.question: When can you drive around railroad crossing gates?

options.text: When other drivers go around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train whistle. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does a reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle mean?
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle's back means it is traveling slower than 25 mph. You may see this on construction equipment, farm vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slow enough so you can stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel hard to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement. Gently apply the brakes to reduce speed. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not make sharp turns to force your vehicle back.

questions.question: A driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light. Who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light. This is true whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.

questions.explanation: Every sudden stop uses fuel when you accelerate back to traffic speed. Look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This improves fuel efficiency.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Always stay at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid traffic buildup.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: When driving on a road with two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering. If the lane next to you is empty, move over.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks at objects off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking to them while driving.
Only watches the vehicle directly in front.

questions.explanation: Do not look at passengers, search for items in your vehicle, read, sightsee, or daydream while driving. Scan the road, check your mirrors, and look at your instrument panel regularly. These safe habits keep you attentive.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must do. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are not permitted.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when anything else makes conditions less than perfect. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are at the posted limit if conditions are unsafe.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be thought of as:

options.text: Safe to cross because a train is unlikely to come.

questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from either direction. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and keep moving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull over to the right curb or side of the road and stop immediately.
